 Writ Petition No.8771 of 2023
Order:

(Per Honourable Sri Justice K. Lakshman) Heard Mr.Naveen Kumar Miryala, learned counsel for the petitioner, and the learned Special Government Pleader for Home, representing the learned Additional Advocate-General, for the respondents.

2. This Writ Petition is filed by the petitioner challenging the detention order passed by the 2nd respondent vide proceedings No.17/PD-CELL/CCRB/RKD/2023, dated 18.03.2023 (for short, 'the impugned detention order') and also the Confirmation Order passed by 1st respondent vide G.O.Rt.No.624, dated 24.04.2023, and to forthwith release the detenu, viz., Mr.Dadi Dharmender Reddy (the father of petitioner herein).
3.

A perusal of the record would go to show that the impugned detention order was issued by the 2nd respondent basing on involvement of detenu in two cases, viz., (i) Crime ::2:: KL,J & PSS,J wp_8771_2023 No.77 of 2023, for offence under Sections 420, 419, 465, 467, 468 and 471 r/w Section 34 of I.P.C. on the file of P.S. Bibinagar; and (ii) Crime No.78 of 2023, for offences under Sections 420, 419, 465, 467, 468 and 471 r/w Section 34 of I.P.C. of P.S. Bibinagar.
4. The allegations levelled against the detenu in both the above crimes are impersonation, forgery and cheating, and that he has created certain fake documents.
According to the 2nd respondent, the detenu is a fake document offender under Section 2(A) of Act 1 of 1986.

5. In the counter-affidavit filed by the 2nd respondent, it is stated that the detenu involved in (16)
crimes during the period from 2011 to 2021.
Though the said (16) crimes were adverted to in the counter-affidavit, they were not relied upon by the 2nd respondent in the impugned detention order.
Therefore, the 2nd respondent cannot improve its version in the counter-affidavit.

Therefore,
according to this Court, the aforesaid (16) cases are stale cases and the detaining authority cannot rely upon the same as per the principle laid down by the Honourable Apex Court in Mohinder Singh Gill vs. The Chief Election ::3:: KL,J & PSS,J wp_8771_2023 Commissioner1 and Khaja Bilal Ahmed Dhadi Shashidhar Reddy vs The State Of Telangana on 20 June, 2023

6.

It is relevant to note that in both the aforesaid two crimes, the Court below has already granted bail to the detenu with certain conditions, including the condition that the detenu shall appear before the Investigating Officer on every Monday between 10:00 a.m. to 02:00 p.m. for a period of two (02) months or till filing of charge-sheet.
According to learned Special Government Pleader for Home, appearing for the respondents, the investigation is pending in the aforesaid two crimes.

7. It is also relevant to note that the Investigating Officer in the above two crimes has not filed any application seeking cancellation of bail granted to the detenu on the ground that detenu had involved in similar offences and also to prevent him from committing similar offences.
Be that as it may, the Investigating Officer had also not even opposed the bail applications filed by the petitioner before the Court below by furnishing information to the learned Public Prosecutor.
1978 A.I.R. 851  2019 SCC Online SC 1657  ::4
: : KL,J & PSS,J
Therefore, without initiating the aforesaid steps, the 2nd respondent cannot issue the impugned detention order.
8. In Ashok Kumar vs. Delhi Administration3, the Honourable Apex Court held that preventive detention is devised to afford protection to society.
The object is to punish a man for having done something but to intercept before he does it, and to prevent him from doing it.

9. In Ram Manohar Lohia vs. State of Bihar4, the Honourable Apex Court held that the detaining authority shall consider the difference between disturbance to public order and that of disturbance to law and order.

sentences.text: 10. The Honourable Apex Court and this Court have, time and again, categorically held that detention orders can be passed in rarest of rare cases, that too, to prevent the detenu from committing similar offence.
11. In the present case, though there is criminal history of the detenu as he had involved in (16) cases earlier, the detaining authority had relied upon only two cases referred above.

sentences.text: The allegations levelled against the detenu are that he had impersonated, forged and created certain fake documents.
Criminal law was also set into motion by the respondents by registering the aforesaid two crimes against the detenu.
Thus, there was no disturbance to the public order of the acts alleged to have been committed by the detenu in the aforesaid crimes.
Further, there was no material placed before the detaining authority to come to subjective satisfaction before issuing the impugned detention order.

12. Therefore, in view of above, this Court is of the opinion that the impugned detention order passed by the 2nd respondent vide proceedings No.17/PD-CELL/CCRB/RKD/2023, dated 18.03.2023 and also the Confirmation Order passed by 1st respondent vide G.O.Rt.No.624, dated 24.04.2023, are liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, they are set aside.
13. The writ petition is allowed.
The respondents are directed to set the detenu, viz., Dadi Dharmender Reddy @ Dharma Reddy, S/o.

Late Narasimha Reddy, Aged : 50 years, Occ : Real ::6::
KL,J & PSS,J wp_8771_2023 Estate Business, R/o.H.No.1-50, Cheeriyal (V), Keesara Mandal,
Medchal District, free forthwith if he is no longer required in any other criminal case.
No costs.
14. As a sequel, miscellaneous applications pending if any in this Writ Petition, shall stand closed.
